not_applied.finding: Section 5 claims no admin route or script calls sendBulkTransactionalEmail, and that no in-product or public notice route exists (header date 2026-10-03).
not_applied.reason: Re-checked in the worktree. The sendBulkTransactionalEmail claim still holds. It is defined at apps/web/lib/support/handoff/resend-client.ts:248. The only other references are tests (apps/web/lib/support/handoff/__tests__/resend-bulk.test.ts, apps/web/lib/services/__tests__/marketing-email-consent.test.ts, apps/web/app/api/settings/team/invitations/__tests__/route.lifecycle.test.ts). Nothing under apps, packages, scripts or services calls it. The in-product notice and public notice claims are partly stale. apps/web/app/api/admin/product-updates/route.ts lets a platform admin write a notification and push to users, but only for a release note picked from a fixed list (findAnnounceableRelease in apps/web/lib/services/product-update-notification-service.ts:43). It cannot carry breach text. apps/web/app/status/page.tsx and apps/web/lib/server/service-notices.ts publish incident and maintenance notices, but not a dated per-incident breach notice at a stable URL. So the runbook is neither clearly right nor clearly wrong on those two points. Rewording it would change a disclosed-limitation statement that the runbook says must stay aligned with apps/web/app/privacy/page.tsx and apps/web/app/privacy/india/page.tsx, which is legal and policy wording. That is a decision for the owner and counsel, not a plain fact fix. I made no edit and left the Last updated line unchanged. Suggested follow-up: have the owner or counsel decide whether the release-announcement route and status notices count as a notice path for breaches, then update §5 and both privacy pages together.
